@billiam @brooke the abs pump issue on Toyota’s like corolla and RAV4 is due to over actuation of the abs system and too much pressure buildup. So the bypass is what makes that really loud pulsing noise. I’ve been testing ways to reduce this affect. I haven’t heard of anyone with a working fix.... if there’s one out there I’d love to know who else is working on it!

[1/16/2019 7:41 AM] Oppey#2151
@jfrux, here is the top **Pull Request** result for **475**...


[1/16/2019 7:41 AM] Oppey#2151


{Embed}
kegman
https://github.com/commaai/openpilot/pull/475
Eliminate brake oscillations and grinding / crunching / ripping sound when using Pedal (Honda Pilot Only) #475
When using the Comma Pedal there are certain situations where the brake makes a very loud grinding / crunching / ripping sound:

a) when OP is engaged and brake is pressed at slow speeds
b) when OP is engaged at standstill and brake is pressed

It was found that when user presses on the brake, brake_pressed does NOT disengage OP until it reaches a threshold value (a dead zone), leading to BOTH the user AND OP applying 2 different brake settings simultaneously.  This leads to an oscillation between the two brake settings rapidly and results in a horrid crunching / grinding / ripping sound.  Additionally the brake lurches and causes an unsafe braking situation.

The fix was to use USER_BRAKE signal (instead of BRAKE_PRESSED) to disengage OP earlier when user depresses the brake pedal and before the oscillation begins.  The logic preserves and covers the brake_pressed scenarios as well.
Number
#475
Status
open
Created
2018-12-20 00:02:29 UTC
Last Update
2018-12-25 01:16:02 UTC
https://images-ext-1.discordapp.net/external/Qe4vKBPCv5W99hZzhnxlO7L3-5KkHDmAkQwI_LYZzwI/https/opc.ai/assets/github-logo.png

[1/23/2019 3:23 PM] jmanl16

[1/23/2019 3:47 PM] j4z_og
The pedal firmware has just a few functions:
1. Read the two analog voltages coming in from the Gas pedal (AtoD) 
2. Write those exact voltages back out to the engine - unaltered if OP doesn't send new signals through CAN (DtoA)
3. Convert the read voltages to numbers and send to CAN (0x201) 
4. Read CAN signals back from OP (0x200) and replace the signals from the Gas Pedal with OP's signals, if engaged.


[1/23/2019 3:49 PM] j4z_og
So the firmware can have problems with one part but not the others. Though this is unlikely. I'm afraid that if we rule everything out but the pedal, it will likely be hardware. 
I built my own Pedal from scratch (soldiered all of those dang tiny components) so I have a good idea of the topology of the thing. The CAN output is basically a chip with a couple resistors that lead to the RJ45 connector. It's possible the chip, resistors, or RJ45 connector are improperly soldered or even bad. 
I'm sure you understand how unlikely all of these issues are, but nevertheless, they are possible.

[3/27/2019 11:47 AM] erichmoraga
@jfrux Your guide worked fine for me...

[4/24/2019 9:30 AM] marcbou3991
but with the pedal it would immediately disengage as soon as it was engaged


[4/24/2019 9:31 AM] marcbou3991
had to increase gas_interceptor_threshold to 15000 in panda/board/safety/safety_honda.h


[4/24/2019 9:32 AM] marcbou3991
and for acceleration to  be smooth had to change INTERCEPTOR_GAS & INTERCEPTOR_GAS2 offsets from -83 to -101 in  the dbc


[4/24/2019 9:32 AM] marcbou3991
now it would be interesting to know if these changes are ok on the pilot 2019


[4/24/2019 9:32 AM] marcbou3991
the diff is at https://github.com/commaai/openpilot/pull/613/files

[4/30/2019 8:45 AM] marcbou3991
I've had a similar problem. If it's a honda pedal, try these workarounds:


[4/30/2019 8:45 AM] marcbou3991
In selfdrive/car/honda/carstate.py:update() find this code section:
263     # this is a hack for the interceptor. This is now only used in the simulation
264     # TODO: Replace tests by toyota so this can go away
265     if self.CP.enableGasInterceptor:
266       self.user_gas = cp.vl["GAS_SENSOR"]['INTERCEPTOR_GAS']
267       print ("user_gas=%f\n" % (self.user_gas))
268       self.user_gas_pressed = self.user_gas > 0 # this works because interceptor read < 0 when pedal position is 0. Once calibrated, this will change


[4/30/2019 8:46 AM] marcbou3991
on the last line (268) above, change self.user_gas > 0 to self.user_gas > 10


[4/30/2019 8:47 AM] marcbou3991
In panda/board/safety/safety_honda.h, change:


[4/30/2019 8:47 AM] marcbou3991
const int gas_interceptor_threshold = 328;


[4/30/2019 8:47 AM] marcbou3991
to


[4/30/2019 8:47 AM] marcbou3991
const int gas_interceptor_threshold = 15000;


[4/30/2019 8:48 AM] marcbou3991
then recompile and re-flash panda firmware (temporarily remove panda from giraffe and connect it to car's OBDII port for this)

[8/2/2019 7:10 AM] wocsor
yeah pedal isn't going to affect your ABS light bro


[8/2/2019 7:11 AM] wocsor
you have an ABS malfunction. can only get that if the VSC is throwing codes. and since it is, then it's going to create new CAN PIDs, which then cause OP to collect a non-matching fingerprint


[8/2/2019 7:13 AM] wocsor
so on top of the ABS light you get all the other errors. solution - see what the code actually is. ABS can throw codes due to anything like worn pads, a dead sensor, steering angle sensor malfunction (part of the VSC), losing comms with any other VSC component...

my bet is you have a bad sensor. cats and rodents like to sneak up under cars and chew on the abs sensor wires. it's like a $30 if you replace it yourself @ron5770

[8/27/2019 6:39 PM] vanillagorillaaa (pinned)
```1. Set the power switch of the Paw to "off".
2. Plug one end of the Paw into the Pedal.
3. Plug the mini-usb to a 5v power source or computer USB.
4. Press and hold the "boot" button of the Paw while turning the switch on.
```

[9/10/2019 9:52 AM] shameed
```python
def transact(self, dat):
    #print "W:",dat.encode("hex")
    self.p.isotp_send(1, dat, 0, recvaddr=2)

    def _handle_timeout(signum, frame):
      # will happen on reset
      raise Exception("timeout")

    signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, _handle_timeout)
    signal.alarm(1)
    try:
      ret = self.p.isotp_recv(2, 0, sendaddr=1)
    finally:
      signal.alarm(0)

    #print "R:",ret.encode("hex")
    return ret
```

[9/12/2019 1:36 PM] wocsor
remember that thing i mentioned about the SPI flasher in the bootstub being busted? here's how it works:


[9/12/2019 1:36 PM] Deleted User
Sorry Just going over some of the history and catching up


[9/12/2019 1:38 PM] shameed
@wocsor haven't got a chance to try out your suggestions.


[9/12/2019 1:38 PM] wocsor
1) you send a special packet over CAN to the pedal, which tells it to enter the bootstub
2) in the bootstub, HW is defined as pedal so it loads the spiflasher and takes in the firmware package over CAN
3) the for loop which actually combines the captured data together has an error where it writes everything to one byte and keeps overwriting. so instead of flashing you just get stuck in bootstub


[9/12/2019 1:39 PM] wocsor
so to fix it you have to reflash the bootstub in DFU mode. incidentally, it will also write the new firmware too


[9/12/2019 1:40 PM] shameed
I see


[9/12/2019 1:40 PM] Deleted User
Seme ELI5 steps on how to do this would be nice. Not an expert on this. Have always used workbench


[9/12/2019 1:40 PM] wocsor
it's kind of a technical explanation but it hopefully will explain why your workbench flashing does not work


[9/12/2019 1:40 PM] shameed
Flashing over USB is the next thing in my list.


[9/12/2019 1:41 PM] shameed
Workbench or manual, it won't work if it keeps on over-writing the same byte instead of collecting byte by byte in a buffer.

[9/12/2019 1:52 PM] shameed
```python
def transact(self, dat):
    #print "W:",dat.encode("hex")
    self.p.isotp_send(1, dat, 0, recvaddr=2)

    def _handle_timeout(signum, frame):
      # will happen on reset
      raise Exception("timeout")

    signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, _handle_timeout)
    signal.alarm(1)
    try:
      ret = self.p.isotp_recv(2, 0, sendaddr=1)
    finally:
      signal.alarm(0)

    #print "R:",ret.encode("hex")
    return ret
```

Coat soldered wires in silicone paste, slide heatshrink over, then heat from center to edges, creating a corrosion-proof seal.


[9/29/2019 3:21 PM] erichmoraga
I'm actually the one who got @wocsor (and in-turn, @brooke) to use harnesses for the Pedals, because I wasn't really happy with the original design.  That said, part of auto-proofing these types of things is to also secure the wires properly with zip-ties if necessary, to prevent premature wear.  One might even consider wrapping the wires in loom to prevent chaffing.


[9/29/2019 3:47 PM] tunderslimer
@Erich i completely agree with this method.  and those reading this will hopefully follow your recommendations.  for prototyping and development, it is my belief that temporary connectors are ok - and once the circuit design is complete a permanent solution implemented.  
I've built entire vehicle harnesses before, I'm certainly not new to automotive electrical design.  I utilize all of the suggestions you made regularly, and so should others. [9/29/2019 3:51 PM] tunderslimer
Hit up amazon though, and check out those self soldering connectors.  If you're US you can probably get a small pack for like $5.  Try them out, you'd be surprised (I was.)  I'm assisting a gps company with deploying 1200 units on food trucks and they needed a way to make secure, sealed connections.  They brought the connectors to me - I tried them out and was pretty surprised at how well they actually worked.  The same rules apply - one must have a heat gun and heat the center first, careful not to burn the heat shrink, then once the solder is viscous move from side to side to seal the connection.


[9/29/2019 3:54 PM] tunderslimer

Maybe in four years I'll be here saying, oh man, don't use those... they wear out/fail/etc etc.  But, they only need to last that long, because the gps units are replaced every three years - and I can fix my jeep anytime I need to.

[10/6/2019 12:35 AM] shameed
Cruise Fault happens with OP from time to time, not very frequently but even without pedal sometimes it happens but very rarely.


[10/6/2019 12:37 AM] shameed
Controls Mismatch only started happening since 0.6.x.  It might have been added in 0.6.x or later 0.5.x.  I think if we press gas and it reads the value back, and compares it with the value that it had set it too (because of pedal being used for gas), it finds a mismatch, so it throws Controls Mismatch alert.


[10/6/2019 12:38 AM] shameed
Our pressing gas causes the gas value to go off, and it doesn't like it, and hence throws the Controls Mismatch exception.


[10/6/2019 12:39 AM] shameed
The gas pressing has to be subtle because otherwise it simply disengages.  If you press slightly enough that it wouldn't disengage it will throw the Controls Mismatch error.

what helped me when i was in that situation was to confirm there is no resistance on a multimeter from each pin on the connector to the corresponding pin on the other connector. This would ensure the "passthrough" functionality of the pedal is working (tests the connectors, connections, board, etc). if each pin shows no resistance, then the car should work as normal

[1/10/2020 8:49 AM] flyboyn222pa
In the future to avoid pinout issues on Honda vehicles. The pedals I sell for for Honda’s will have the Honda connectors attached on one side and the pedal molex terminals crimped on the other, but I won’t install the terminals in the molex plug housing. Due to the various Honda pinouts this will prevent errors from happening and will guarantee that most Honda vehicles will be compatible with the pedals I sell.


[1/10/2020 8:50 AM] flyboyn222pa
All you have to do when you get the pedal is push the terminals into the housing according to your vehicles pinout and push the molex plug into the socket on the board.

OP can send brake commands down to 0, but as soon as it tries to send a gas command the ECU says "ha no" and OP has to abort


[1/29/2020 8:21 PM] tikibug

[2/3/2020 11:45 AM] flyboyn222pa
@andreijikh the connectors on the car side are already wired. All you have to do is figure out the pinout of your car and trace the wires back to the board. All the connections are labeled on the board. 1,2,5V,gnd. Once you know where the wires go simply insert them into the molex connector on the pedal side.

If you need help figuring out which wire is which from your car you’ll have to talk to the other Toyota guys. I specifically don’t wire pedals for specific cars because they are all different.

[2/7/2020 6:04 PM] .runchman
@anthony.flores. if you can drive it without the RJ45 connected, that's the first test, if that works it means the code and wiring is ok. So make sure that works consistently. If it then goes crazy with the RJ45 connected, that might be the same issue as mine. I had signals 1 and 2 apparently backwards from what the s/w expected. In the DBC file there's scaling factors on the 2 signals, like .125 on one and .25 on the other...I flipped those around, problem solved. FIRST though make sure it works fine without the RJ45, to verify your connectors are good and that code in the pedal is running.

[2/11/2020 12:09 AM] tunderslimer
***THE ORDER IS NOT IMPORTANT***
***ONLY THE COLORS ARE, IN ANY SCHEMATIC I SHARE.***


[2/11/2020 12:10 AM] tunderslimer
Follow the colors. If pink is 5v, make sure it's going to a 5v pin on the pedal.


[2/11/2020 12:11 AM] tunderslimer
The numbers, as they appear in the wiring diagrams, could be position numbers. It varies from manufacturer to manufacturer.


[2/11/2020 12:12 AM] tunderslimer
***DO NOT RELY ON POSITION NUMBERS IN THE WIRING DIAGRAMS.***


[2/11/2020 12:18 AM] tunderslimer
If you don't understand how to read the diagram, please ask. I will help you interpret the wires. They will always be some combination of two 5v wires, two ground wires, and two signal wires.


[2/11/2020 12:23 AM] tunderslimer
BRN, GRY = 5v
WHT, WHT = GND
YEL = SIG A(1)
PUR = SIG B(2)


[2/11/2020 12:24 AM] tunderslimer
@doktor it appears that yes... The order for that particular car does in fact match up with the pic you made. 
So, you should be ok.

[2/15/2020 1:36 PM] doktor_sleepless
Anyway, I think I at least figured out a solution for those people getting stuck in "flashing obj/comma.bin." when trying to flash pedal over CAN even with car on. I ended having go through the same process I went through for flashing my EPS firmware with black planda (HT CFranHonda).  I don't know why it worked. It just did.   
1.    pkill -f boardd in /panda
2.    Comment out CFLAGS += "-DEON" in build.mk  in /panda/board
3.    Reflash Panda. For me, I had to run both “make” and then “make recover” in /board to get the next step working
4.    In /panda, run PYTHONPATH=~/panda python3 -c "from python import Panda; Panda().set_safety_mode(17)"  (Lights start to alternately change color without blinking for me)
5.    Run update pedal firmware on workbench.

[3/11/2020 3:13 PM] tunderslimer
since you have a multimeter it should be fairly easy to identify the wires... you'll have two showing 5v, two grounds (0.000 ohms to ground), and two signal wires that will vary between 4-240ish ohms depending on the pedal position


[3/11/2020 3:13 PM] noillek
Damn pedal 🤣


[3/11/2020 3:13 PM] tunderslimer
the signal wires will change relative to their corresponding grounds, the 5v doesn't matter, but the signal and grounds are matched pairs

[3/14/2020 6:01 PM] voltag37174
@JMPZ11 what  @runchman says sounds valid.  The load the factory pedal puts on the sensor lines is around 200kohm but the pedal board has 2kohm.  So you can either try substituting the 10k resistors from R1-R4 or order some 100k,0.1% resistors.  The problem with trying to correct it in software is that the voltage differential shows the signal lines are not capable of driving a 2k load so you can't rely on the linearity of the measured voltages.

@Voltag3 my apologies but something else occurred to me that you might find amusing I don't know. They did not set up the compilation of the firmware to include floating point numbers. [4/11/2020 10:41 AM] perchderpkins
Is anyone using a 2017 or 2018 Corolla with a pedal on stock OP? Everytime I use stock OP with my pedal I get a steering temporarily unavailable error until it faults cruise control completely. Arne's fork fixed this, but I quickly switched back to stock OP. I saw Arne had a fix for this in January, but merging the change with stock OP is not fixing the issue.


[4/14/2020 5:16 PM] perchderpkins
In the event anyone wondered what my issue was or if in the future someone is searching for a similar issue. The Panda safety code is a little too sensitive about gas presses. My pedal's gas sensor was being detected as pressed even when my foot was not near it. This cause the Panda to trigger a safety violation, which causes OP to fault as well. Hopefully my request is upstreamed soon.

[5/1/2020 10:53 AM] tunderslimer
DO NOT RELY ON THE NUMBERS.  they may, by some miracle, work, but don't use them.  Rely on the COLORS only.  
VCPx = 5V
EPAx = GND
VPAx = SIGNALS
if you get funky behavior, aka, accel warning lights, swap the signal wires only, don't worry about 5V and GND.  Put WHT where RED was, and RED where WHT was.

[5/6/2020 5:14 PM] flyboyn222pa
@Willis1 while it is far more likely that the wiring got screwed up as opposed to the board failing. You can check the board operation by plugging it into a normal USB port. If the light blinks rapidly the board is probably fine, I would check the wiring. If the light does not blink rapidly then there is actually a fault. I will gladly replace the board for you. [5/19/2020 9:23 AM] flyboyn222pa
@kamran nothing you received was damaged. The anti-static bag has to be opened because I have to solder the molex connectors to the board. I suppose the alternative is letting you guys solder your own connections. I also can’t place the PCB in the case because you guys need to complete the pinout wiring by inserting the Pins in the Molex connectors which you can’t do with the case assembled. I’ve never had a board fail during shipping and the one board that was returned to me I re-flashed and sent back to the customer so likely user error. I want everyone to know that my pedals are made by a professional PCB manufacturer with a modern pick and place machine. They aren’t hand made so the probability that a board is faulty is incredibly low.  I don’t try to figure out the pinouts for every Honda out there so I leave it to the customer to complete the wiring and the reason is fairly evident in this thread. I don’t have all the cars to test with and literally this entire thread is people trying to figure out which model has what pinout. Honda changes pinouts by both model and model year, and the Honda OP community has so much bad advice out there about pedal pinouts that I decided I didn’t want to be responsible for shorting out someone’s car because from the outside looking in its impossible to figure out what’s correct and what’s not. I have no problem with you returning the pedal because I have a 30 day return policy, but I want the community to know that the product you received was not faulty and you simply decided that you weren’t comfortable installing a pedal, which is perfectly fine by me. Refund will head your way when I get the pedal in the mail.

[5/19/2020 9:33 AM] flyboyn222pa
Yes. All the pedal does is take and input voltage across the two channels and alter it if necessary then output two voltages to the car. The only difference between cars is the slope of voltage curves across the channels as the pedal is pressed. The physical hardware will likely work but you’ll likely have to flash you own firmware.

Wire coloring is more likely to change than pinouts.   Look at the explanation below the picture about what the signals mean then follow the pinout numbers 1-6 as shown. Corresponding Signals are marked on the PCA (printed circuit assembly) from flyboy.  “IN” side on PCA connects to pedal sensor, other side to vehicle harness.

[7/12/2020 9:26 AM] bugsyborromeo
So with Camrys and CHRs
- Most Toyotas send the ACC message through the camera which the panda filters away or through the DSU which can be unplugged
- - Camry and CHR are unique in that the radar sends the ACC message.

Solutions:
1. Unplug the radar so that OP can send its own message (similar to unplugging the DSU. However, this means you lose the accuracy of using radar and must rely on vision which currently has some downfalls.
2. Disable the ACC message from being sent by the radar by putting it in some diagnostic mode, fault state or similar (hasn't been figured out yet) or use a second "proxy panda" to filter out this message. This allows openpilot to send the ACC message without conflicting with the stock message

Using a pedal can be used to resume from a stop or maybe increase your acceleration when paired with stock ACC.
DM me if you wanna discuss further, I'd like to see it happen since we have a camry as well but I just don't have time to work on it

[7/25/2020 9:22 PM] jolly99.
@cellfreak panda paws are obsolete. Make some comma keys. Just replace big usb connector with an usb-c one. Disconnect GND from the shield and connect it to the push button, like it is on panda paw. You will need D+, D-, V-bus, GND and shield to be wired up. I also got 12 pcbs and a friend convinced me to make them. More chances to sell them and more margin ($99 instead of $20).


[7/25/2020 9:36 PM] jolly99.
@JMPZ11 Eon or Comma2 is the easiest  development platform someone can use. Everything is there and working... You can compile pedal code there, scp it to your laptop and flash pedal over usb. A panda paw can be used to put it in DFU mode. Easiest debug method is to use a CAN monitor and look for activity (id 201). To test ad/da part, connect a potentiometer on the pedal port and look of the copy of input voltage on the output port.

[7/28/2020 2:34 PM] adobo07527
PEDAL ISSUES FIXED:


[7/28/2020 2:39 PM] adobo07527
There were a lot of different things I have tried, from replacing cables to reflashing. But at the end of the day, when I wasn't getting any errors from the C2 or the pedal ... it had to be connection. I made sure my harness was secure and then checked the OBDII Port. That turned out to be the issue. My C2 was working just fine. I had the car running (in drive but break on) when I unplugged and plugged back in the OBDII Port. All of a sudden the "No seatbelt" error came on the C2 when I tried to engage. This is when I new I had a good connection. After a quick drive, I had confirmed the Pedal was working again.

[8/21/2020 4:37 PM] priusprime.
what is the difference between a pedal and SDSU?


[8/21/2020 8:22 PM] perchderpkins
@PriusPrime A pedal emulated your accelerator pedal to allow cars that can not use cruise control from 0 MPH to accelerate after stopping. A SDSU allows your car (Toyota) to brake down to 0 MPH.


[8/21/2020 8:59 PM] priusprime.
Thank you for the clarity


[8/22/2020 11:42 PM] johhansan
> @PriusPrime A pedal emulated your accelerator pedal to allow cars that can not use cruise control from 0 MPH to accelerate after stopping. A SDSU allows your car (Toyota) to brake down to 0 MPH.
@PerchDerpkins  does getting a pedal makes the acc that don't work under certain speed completely break to 0 MPH?  I always thought that you only needed the pedal for stop and go acc.


[8/23/2020 8:05 AM] perchderpkins
@Johhan No. The pedal only connects to your gas pedal. The only fix I know of for cars that don't brake down to zero is unplugging the DSU, but this is Toyota based. I am not sure about other cars and how they may bypass the limits of ACC.

With toyota ss2.0 you will not need a SDSU. With pre-2019(?) you will need a SDSU and ZSS (to help with steering).

[9/14/2020 3:49 AM] debbor
@Johhan the pin-1 designator for the STM is the colored-in triangle at the top-right of the footprint, so they have that wrong.
J4 looks to be a wired connector. These need to be crimped to wires and then soldered to the through-hole pads on the board


[9/14/2020 8:07 AM] johhansan
@DebboR what can I tell them or do to fix this?


[9/14/2020 8:08 AM] debbor
Just tell them to use the triangle as the 1st pin designator, and if possible, crimp and solder the connectors yourself. That's usually not something PCB manufacturers would do

{Reactions}
👍

[9/14/2020 9:21 AM] carlos_ddd
And be careful about Pin1 marking and the injection-mold-point of the STM32 housing. Those can be easily confused! Look at the datasheet to verify which one is pin1 ...

Your traction control will take a little while to sync up and report in good (Usually about 5 miles and then turn your car off/on). Basically your accelerator pedal was reporting in incorrect, so the car disabled traction control until the system looks correct. It is a safety feature.

[9/23/2020 2:40 PM] perchderpkins
Measure the in and out voltage of the pedal. It is outputting voltages, which control acceleration. A test is to power it from an Arduino. The voltages should ideally be extremely close to zero if I remember correctly. You can then use 3.3V for example from the Arduino to provide voltage and see if it passes to the corresponding signal in.

[12/21/2020 3:32 PM] heymynameisivan
Does one need both a s-dsu AND pedal to enable stop and go / OP long? or just one or the other? how far does JUST the pedal get you on tssp>


[12/21/2020 4:09 PM] techbaumgartner
Hi @heymynameisivan#0658 

Here are my notes for an '18 Toyota Corolla

If you wanted to try the OP Long. In a safe off-road location, You can disconnect the DSU and enable community features and you will have OP Long enabled, this will slow you down to 0 mph. Disconnecting the DSU removes Automated Emergency Braking.

With the DSU disconnected you can add a comma pedal to enable acceleration from a stop. Off road use only.

If you add an S-DSU with your comma pedal, you re-enable the Automated Emergency Braking while being able to have full stop and go.  

Hope that helps! I tried to show you the different levels. Let me know if you have any questions 👍

[2/14/2021 7:15 AM] starlogfl
Using any Distro of Linux get dfu-util as the program to run:
As root with the USB cable plugged into the pedal and 5v applied to the feed thru  for 3 seconds, then release the 5v. type:
Lsusb
The result should show:
Bus 001 Device 009: ID 0483:df11 STMicroelectronics STM Device in DFU Mode
If you want to rip the current binary out of the pedal do this:

sudo ./dfu-util -d , -a 0 -s 0x08000000 -U filename.bin
The file will be saved with the filename you give it.
You can look at the file with xxd filename
If you have a good binary file you want to flash, this is the command:
sudo ./dfu-util -d , -a 0 -s 0x08000000:leave -D filename.bin
The process to get into DFU mode is to put the 5v on that feed thru for about 3 seconds, some times you have to do it 2 or 3 times.
To verify, once you remove the 5v, and hit enter to write the file, you will see a grogress bar.
Downloading to address = 0x08000000, size = 65536
Download    [=========================] 100%        65536 bytes

[3/26/2021 7:46 PM] mlocoteta
Alright so I'm looking to add pedal support to the 2016/2017 accord- a few things seem off. 

When plugging the pedal in, the "INTERCEPTOR_GAS2" hovers around -46 and "INTERCEPTOR_GAS" hovers around 69/70 when my foot is off the pedal.

When following the carstate formula:
`self.user_gas = (cp.vl["GAS_SENSOR"]['INTERCEPTOR_GAS'] + cp.vl["GAS_SENSOR"]['INTERCEPTOR_GAS2']) / 2.` it's very clear that       `self.user_gas_pressed = self.user_gas > 1e-5  # this works because interceptor read < 0 when pedal position is 0. Once calibrated, this will change` is true, which forces OP to think the gas is pressed. 

What is the "correct" way to deal with this dependency? Editing the self.user_gas value (increase 1e-5?) or applying offsets to the DBC file? ( I copied this from the 2016ILX pedal and posted below for convince). I really couldn't find much on this topic in the pins or search history, so any advice would be appreciated.

And yes- the pedal functions as the stock pedal fine.

If openpilot can control the ACC function it will do has a brakes. The pedal adds the ability for openpilot to command the resume function from a stop, which some cars don’t natively support. If openpilot cannot control ACC on your car then a pedal won’t do anything for you

[8/8/2021 1:14 PM] mlocoteta
I just wanted to mention- looking at most of these splitter (amazon i.e. ) there isn't any indication of the wiring and I've actually bought 2 different ones which look completely different that both burned up on me. And the sad part is when it does burn up it can destroy a lot of suff (fuses don't blow but the ethernet wire melts). I've had to replace my harness box because of this (ethernet connector fused to harness box RJ45). 
 I noticed @tinybear didn't mention it but it looks like he's selling the right version on his etsy https://www.etsy.com/listing/1018215440/splitter-for-comma-pedal?ref=related-1&frs=1

I'm not really trying to shill but moreso trying to warn everyone about buying the right splitter type.  I can post pictures of the burn wiring from using the "wrong" ethernet haha. I'd say if you get you own be very sensitive when you plug it in, or use a RJ45 tester to confirm pin 1-pin1, pin2-pin2, etc.

{Reactions}
😆

[8/8/2021 1:15 PM] mlocoteta
mine looked identical to this, so even if it "looks" right, without testing on a network tester or having a explicit wiring diagram, it's hard to tell

`#!/usr/bin/env python3
from panda import Panda
from opendbc.can.packer import CANPacker

dbc_name ='toyota_nodsu_hybrid_pt_generated'
packer = CANPacker(dbc_name)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    p = Panda()
    p.set_safety_mode(Panda.SAFETY_ALLOUTPUT)
    dumpsafety = p.health()
    print(f"\nsafety_mode: {dumpsafety['safety_mode']}")
    print("If safety mode == 0? so ALLOUTPUT don't worked OR FLAG ALLOWDEBUG is missing\non Panda flash")

    while True:
        for ac_Voltage in range(-20, 20):
            values = {
            "ACCEL_CMD": ac_Voltage, 
            }

            data = packer.make_can_msg("ACC_CONTROL", 0, values)
            pedal_bus = 4 # comma_pedal ins on bus 4?
            print(data)
            p.can_send(data[0], data[2], pedal_bus)

[9/4/2021 1:39 PM] perchderpkins
The ESP off message on your device is a sign the PCM is not getting a accelerator pedal value it likes. It will often happen for a brief moment and be fine, but it is a sign that you are going to get a traction control fault soon. You have to hold the pedal down completely confirms a connection issue. Rather than leave you stranded Toyota will allow if you mash the pedal down for acceleration to work in a limited capacity. I have the issue every 6 months and replace the connector. If I try to just resolder the connector in my experience it comes back within a week.

{Reactions}
👍

[9/4/2021 1:43 PM] perchderpkins
While it is a questionable fix I have tried multiple pedals from different people, connections, etc. and it always comes back in about 6 months.


[9/4/2021 1:44 PM] perchderpkins
I will say I noticed it is always the connector on the ECU side that is the issue in my case. The connector that goes to the accelerator pedal itself is not the issue because in Cabana I can see the stable gas sensor inputs.

[12/17/2021 3:03 PM] tin._.tin
Hi. I have a Toyota pedal and recently it's causing check engine light code p2138. Removing the pedal doesn't cause engine light anymore. Do we have any guides on debugging this?


[12/17/2021 3:06 PM] tin._.tin


{Attachments}
https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/524595554898935808/921508575036186654/6DFB6754-DB7F-4B27-963A-FA77E03FDEE9.jpg?ex=6a62823d&is=6a6130bd&hm=75055f9c1efbe955989d389a73f50cb95680b9354e998d40977f031fbc8947e0&


[12/17/2021 9:03 PM] perchderpkins
That means your car is not getting the proper signals from your pedal. The most common is it will only be getting one signal. For safety, accelerators have two signals to allow one fault to be caught and handled. An easy way to test this is send some low voltage to input 1 and see what output 1 has. Then do two (Or both together - Make sure to scale voltage differently between them). That should help you isolate where your connection issue is.


[12/17/2021 11:17 PM] tin._.tin
Thank you


[12/18/2021 8:35 AM] charchil10
It happened to me too. Changing connectors worked for me! Good luck! Most probably its connector issue!

[2/7/2022 7:52 PM] tinybear_
I checked with my oscilloscope last night and it isn't simple as just add a cap. Beside, op amp is not good at driving large impedance circuit directly. What I found out is that the power source has 200mV Vpp and this cause op amp to have 1.2V Vpp. My plan is to add a cap not at output side but at power source side.


[2/7/2022 7:53 PM] tinybear_
But this is just my guess for now. Will update when more data is available.


[2/7/2022 8:46 PM] jlundstrom

[5/17/2022 1:26 PM] nworby
Would you be able to elaborate on what you did to resolve this? I'm having the same issue. Could this be fixed in hardware by swapping the two data wires on the pedal board?


[5/17/2022 10:20 PM] nworby
Figured it out. For anyone in the future who has this problem:
1. Edit `opendbc/generator/<your_make>/_comma.dbc`. Use the opendbc readme to guide you in what changes to make. I had to log some values and use a bit of algebra to find correct scaling/shifting parameters
2. Run `PYTHONPATH=/data/openpilot opendbc/generator/generator.py`
3. Reboot

{Reactions}
👍 (2)

[5/18/2022 12:25 PM] alesatobrazilsp
@IceyJ (2021 Sienna)


[5/18/2022 1:16 PM] iceyj
Is this for the sienna?


[5/18/2022 1:40 PM] nworby
No, Chevy Volt. The process should be roughly the same to tune your dbc parameters though. More detailed instructions as follows:
1. Go on a drive where you have your foot off the pedal as well as flooring the pedal. (For me, it's fine to just do this while parked and idling.)
2. Go to cabana and paste in the file `opendbc/generator/<your_make>/_comma.dbc`, changing the `INTERCEPTOR_GAS` and `INTERCEPTOR_GAS2` scaling parameters to `(1,0)` for both.
3. Read the min and max values on the graph. Should correspond to when your foot was off the pedal and when you were flooring it.
4. For each of the two interceptor, solve the following system of equations to get the correct scaling (a) and shift (b) parameters `(a,b)`:
    {min}a+b=0
    {max}a+b=255
5. Update `_comma.dbc` file with the new values, run generation script and reboot

[6/25/2022 3:15 PM] nworby
Could be either a tuning or DBC issue on OP side or a FW issue on the pedal side. I'd start with seeing if it's a DBC issue personally. To do that:
1. Record a drive (your car can be stationary) where you floor the pedal at some point
2. Open recording in cabana
3. Import the DBC file from `generator/honda/_comma.dbc` and see if the points on the graph corresponding to max gas take values of ~255

To see if it's a tuning issue, try increasing your long ki values in `interface.py`. Idk how to deal with pedal FW but hopefully this is a helpful starting point. Happy to elaborate in DM if need be

[6/30/2022 11:49 AM] nworby
A little bit more complicated than a config file but still doable if you know nothing about coding:
1. Clone openpilot repo (or fork)
2. Open `selfdrive/car/<your_make>/interface.py`, ctrl+f for `kiV`. 
3. Increase the values in this list by a little bit
4. Upload to your car via SSH (you should be able to find a guide on how to do this by searching this discord, or someone else can help you)

[10/1/2022 5:46 PM] nworby
No harness changes needed, although if the harness for your car connects via RJ45 (ethernet) to the OBD2 port then you'll need an RJ45 splitter. 

In general, unless you have an EV, you won't get braking by using a pedal interceptor, and even then it will be limited. I finally got around to updating my car to use the new end-to-end long and it makes that issue almost negligible. Definitely 10x more useful than it was before.


[10/1/2022 10:36 PM] bboydreidel
New end to end long? What is that? Interesting, so usually only cars that have acc already will be able to do it with op


[10/2/2022 8:15 AM] nworby
Previously openpilot handled gas and brakes like glorified ACC. Now it's model-based so drives much more like a human. In my experience, this makes braking restrictions not as much of an issue -- for instance, it will (mostly) coast to a stop behind cars piled up at a red light, instead of continuing along at 40mph until you're only a few yards away then trying to brake

[1/28/2023 7:50 PM] gadjex
That code doesn't need to be messed with to help with smooth stops. In interface.py, under you car model add
 ret.vEgoStopping = 0.15
 ret.stoppingDecelRate = 0.3

See: https://github.com/commaai/cereal/blob/master/car.capnp#L463

The 0.2 seconds is: if you are at a stop for a period of time, pulse the brake pump 0.2 seconds every 20 seconds to keep pressure on the brakes incase there is a small bleed off of pressure.


[1/28/2023 7:58 PM] gadjex
That part of the code also turns on the brake pump anytime more brake pressure is needed. If you don't know what you are doing don't change this code.

[6/20/2023 7:51 PM] isoseller
Hi, I was told that in order for the comma 3 to work on my 2023 Bolt EUV (No premier, no supercruise), I would need a pedal. Could someone explain what this means and what the pedal does?


[6/20/2023 8:02 PM] nworby
When you press the accelerator in your car, it sends signals as voltages across some wires to the ECU. A pedal interceptor can electronically mimic these signals, so your car "thinks" that you are pressing the pedal, when in reality you're not. Openpilot uses this to control accel/decel. Note that on Bolt, we cannot control friction brakes this way, so you are limited to regenerative braking. You don't *need* a pedal interceptor for your car, as there are ways to get limited speed control without it, but it's well worth the money.

Do double check that your car does not have adaptive cruise control, as some 2LT trim Bolts do. If you have ACC, you do not need a pedal (though it is still helpful, see https://discord.com/channels/469524606043160576/524611823090008065/1120835202730688512)

{Reactions}
✅

Wondering if there's a particular splitter you recommend?  Thanks!


[10/12/2023 2:46 AM] tinybear_
You need to find splitter with this schematic: https://discord.com/channels/469524606043160576/524595554898935808/888507881647898687
Normal ethernet splitter works by dividing pins 1-4 and 5-8 and reorder them which is not what we want.


[10/12/2023 2:48 AM] tinybear_
In your case, you need splitter for Comma power (OBD port) -> splitter,  splitter -> pedal, splitter -> harness box.

{Reactions}
👍

[10/12/2023 2:48 AM] tinybear_
Order of connection does not matter.

[1/22/2024 9:41 AM] knight_industries_2k
As far as I know pedal is for vehicles without stop and go functionality and you need that feature with openpilot. And it's irrespective of whether it's EON or Comma 3 (And I also believe for Openpilot to work vehicle anyway need ACC functionality)
The thing is not all vehicles have same ACC functionality. Some only enables to engage it at higher velocities like above 25mph/40kmh however these vehicles can bring the vehicle to a gradual stop in case of traffic ahead slows and stops but just can't accelerate from standstill through ACC. Thus, making comma pedal required to emulate acceleration through pedal if you need stop and go functionality with openpilot. Even in this case if you are fine with using openpilot only at higher speeds you of course you still don't need comma pedal. 
Some vehicles come equipped with ACC with stop and go functionality they don't need comma pedal.

[4/13/2025 3:03 PM] tinybear_
## Pedal Update Apr-2025
Thanks for the community effort. There are some updates on the pedal firmware.
### Bolt 17-21: 
A new update was released in early 2025. If you purchased a pedal from the Beartech workshop before Jan 15th, 2025, you should consider updating your firmware with the latest tune. 
The firmware is available here: https://github.com/fraserxiong/panda_firmware/tree/NEW-bolt17-21_pedal_firmware
You don't need to flash the firmware again if you have done it after Aug 4th, 2024.

{Forwarded Message}
the five minute timer is after five minutes of holding hydraulically with the ESP module (ABS pump) it handsover to the EPB to maintain the hold for however else long. 

"the esp module in the car requires accelerator input before the EPB can be reset/raised? therefore unless there is a way to signal accelerator input you cannot override the behaviour - hence hardware comma pedal is required to provide the signal. ?", pretty much, yes, once EPB engages after 5 minute timer you can no longer auto resume, therefore comma cannot either. 

"Has anyone installed a comma pedal in MQB with ACC sng to test this as a valid approach ?", yes, I own one, I said this in my original question, this is validated behavior. If you want you can test it by pressing "OK" or "RES" once the EPB engages after holding behind a lead vehicle for 5 mins+

[6/15/2026 7:14 AM] crewskedgm
What’s the 2x9 harness box mean??

I ordered my Comma Four with the Honda Nidec harness. I see YouTube videos online that I will require Ethernet cable? Is this still the case? Cuz it seems my harness doesn’t even take Ethernet


[6/15/2026 7:23 AM] tinybear_
An Ethernet cable is still required if you want to use the pedal.
The harness box connects the harness and the USB-C cable from C4. 
The 2x9 harness box has an Ethernet port that connects the pedal to the harness box. The harness box from Comma no longer has an Ethernet port. 
More details here:https://docs.innoisle.com/beartech/harness-and-harness-box-description
